chunks: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'When Marwan was born, they presented him to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) to supplicate for him. So they sent him to Ayesha so that she would supplicate for him. When she brought him near him, he (peace be upon him) said, “Take him away from me, the lizard, son of the lizard.” Zurara said, “And I do not know except that he said, and cursed him.”'

key_terms.أَبُو جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), referring to Imam Muhammad al-Baqir
key_terms.الْوَزَغَ: The lizard, used here as a metaphor for the Umayyads
key_terms.عَائِشَةَ: Ayesha bint Abi Bakr, wife of the Prophet
key_terms.مَرْوَانُ: Marwan ibn al-Hakam, a prominent Umayyad caliph

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about Marwan when he was presented as an infant?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (as) recounts how the Prophet Muhammad (saww) identified the infant Marwan ibn al-Hakam as 'the lizard, son of the lizard,' a metaphor for the Banu Umayya's cunning and eventual rise to power. This incident is historically significant in Shia scholarship as an early prophetic declaration of the Umayyad caliphate's character, with the 'lizard' symbolizing their agility in seizing authority and their distinct lineage from the Quraysh. The addition of 'and cursed him' underscores the divine disapproval of their rule, linking their political ascent to spiritual deviation.
